name: Abstract Motion Graphics (Motion Design and Cinematography category; explicit provenance, directly named in source).
visualIdentity: Explicit: a continuous visual system built from a few shapes and limited colors, with deliberate proportions and centers of gravity. Repetition, division, merging, rotation, and varied timing let each state lead into the next. Unrelated particles or light effects are excluded to protect the structural motif.
suitableUses: Explicit: the source lists this as a good fit for abstract motion work. Example combinations suggest brand idents, loop backgrounds, abstract section transitions, music visuals, and event openers. Inferred: it suits topics where shape logic itself carries the message. Specific client sectors are unspecified.
limitations: Explicit: shape vocabulary must stay within the primary motif set. Avoid crossfades presented as morphs, unrelated particles or glow, rapid full-frame flashing on beats, and live randomness that breaks seekability. Reading text is unspecified beyond palette contrast checks. Secondary styles only when materials and movement stay compatible.
palette: Suggested, not supplied: background #F6F0E2, foreground #283D47, accent_1 #458784, accent_2 #D28456. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background measures 9.997 and meets the normal text target. Accents fail for body text (3.658 and 3.881) and are decorative only. Approved task colors override these; never recolor or auto-darken them.
motionAndInteraction: Video motion must derive from composition time with varied timing and repeated, rotating, or merging shape states. Shared guidance favors smooth authored movement but preserves deliberate cuts, impacts, and reading holds. Interactive delivery is optional and inferred from examples: morphs on hover or section change, scrubbable timelines, and a static reduced-motion state.
audio: Explicit: no fixed soundtrack, genre, tempo, or mandatory audio layer is required. Suggested option: music-synchronized accents where repetition counts change on downbeats, driven by a precomputed beat map rather than live analysis. If voiceover is added, speech must stay intelligible, unclipped, and free of competing vocals. Music choice is otherwise unspecified.
assetRequirements: Explicit: no external assets are mandated; the system is built from reusable shape groups and shared coordinates. Fonts and any imported assets must load before rendering. Morphing needs contour-matched geometry with consistent point order. Topic or brand assets are unspecified, and missing assets should be reported rather than invented.
combinations: Explicit: style-100 (contour-matched morphs with traceable form lineage and fixed color roles per shape family) and style-105 (musical section timing driving density and division) are the suggested hybrids. Abstract Motion Graphics is described as strongest alone as a self-contained shape system. Hybrids are optional and should avoid particles or glow unrelated to the motif.
productionApproach: Explicit: HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for composition, seekable timing, audio sync, validation, and export; Remotion is fallback only when a documented limitation applies. SVG is the suggested style renderer, GSAP the suggested paused seekable motion engine. Optional tools include p5.js, Paper.js, Anime.js, mo.js, and Delaunator. Verify seeks, decoded frames, and palette fidelity.
